Thanks for the ping, Dylan — saw the questionnaire and skimmed the answers. High-level guidance: 

- Roles: agree that for the pilot Redwood will be a processor; include clear language in the DPA that Horizon is controller for customer data and that Redwood processes under documented instructions.

- SCC module: Module 3 (Controller-to-Processor plus onward processing clauses) is appropriate for their use case because they flagged onward transfers and multi-jurisdiction processing. Our standard DPA references the standard SCCs but does not automatically include Module 3-specific clauses. We should: 
  a) Offer their legal team the standard DPA + SCC selection form and propose a Module 3 addendum.
  b) Expect minor redlines around audit rights and subprocessor notification timelines.

- HIPAA/BAA: Redwood does not currently execute BAAs as standard in hosted plans. We can support HIPAA with a dedicated Private deployment + BAA as part of an enterprise contract. For now, confirm to them that the pilot should avoid PHI until we have legal approval and BAA in place.

- Questionnaire ownership: Laura / Trust team should own the formal questionnaire response and provide the completed answers back to the customer. I’ll help where there are security-specific controls (SOC 2 evidence).

Next steps I propose (owners & ETA):
- Laura: finalize questionnaire answers and return to Horizon (ETA: 48 business hours from receipt).
- Legal (Marissa): prepare Module 3 SCC addendum draft and review DPA redlines (ETA: 3 business days).
- Dylan: share proposed timeline with Horizon and flag the pilot PHI constraint.

Attachments: scc_module_options.pdf (summary for legal), note: I attached the SOC 2 snapshot you already shared.

I’ll join the Friday 30m if you schedule it.

—
Ben Carter
Head of Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
